cards.explanation: Verify the ingredients with the head chef, isolate with designated equipment for any replacement, escalate to a manager, and document the incident.
cards.why_it_matters: Allergen complaints are medical, not a service issue.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, allergen and safety complaints

cards.prompt: A guest thinks a dish contained their allergen but says they feel fine. What now?
options: Wait to see if they feel unwell
Involve a manager now and log it
answer: Involve a manager now and log it
cards.explanation: Involve a manager immediately, however minor the guest makes it sound, and log the incident even if no reaction occurred.
cards.why_it_matters: Reactions can start later, and the log helps stop it happening again.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, allergen and safety complaints

cards.prompt: Who confirms the ingredients of a dish for a guest with an allergy?
cards.explanation: Always verify allergens with the head chef. Never guess.
cards.why_it_matters: The head chef knows every recipe and any change made today.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, service do's and don'ts; Operations Manual v2026/01, allergen protocol

cards.prompt: A guest complains and you want to give a discount. What's the rule?
options: Get manager authorisation; no need to log it
Log the reason yourself and apply it
Get manager authorisation, with a logged reason
Give up to 10% yourself, then tell the manager
answer: Get manager authorisation, with a logged reason
cards.explanation: All voids and discounts need manager authorisation and a logged reason, even to solve a complaint.
cards.why_it_matters: It protects you, the guest and the business.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, void and discount controls; Operations Manual v2026/01, void and discount controls
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: When should an order be entered into the POS?
options: Once the whole table has ordered
When you pick up the next order
cards.explanation: Every order goes into the POS immediately, so errors are caught at order stage, not at billing.
cards.why_it_matters: The kitchen starts cooking sooner and the bill is right.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, POS accuracy
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Put the LEARN steps for handling a complaint in order.
cards.explanation: LEARN: Listen, Empathise, Apologise, Resolve, Notify.
cards.why_it_matters: The same calm steps every time turn a complaint into loyalty.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, the LEARN recovery method

cards.prompt: In LEARN, what does the N (Notify) step mean?
options: Note it on the guest's bill
Tell the kitchen what went wrong
Follow up, and log the issue
answer: Follow up, and log the issue
cards.explanation: Notify: follow up to confirm the guest is satisfied, and log the issue so it doesn't happen again.
cards.why_it_matters: Logging it is how the team fixes the cause, not just the table.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, the LEARN recovery method
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest is complaining. While they speak, what do you do?
options: Apologise and offer to replace the dish
Explain what happened in the kitchen
Reassure them it won't happen again
cards.explanation: Listen first: give full attention and don't interrupt, explain or defend. Let the guest finish.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests want to be heard before anything else.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, the LEARN recovery method
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (sample of 10), drafted by Claude 16 Oct 2026. Same facts and right answer; the new wrong options come from our own menus and standards.

cards.prompt: Which phrase should you avoid with an unhappy guest?
options: "Let me get this sorted for you immediately."
"Thank you for telling me, let me make this right."
cards.explanation: Avoid phrases like "That's not my section" or "There's nothing I can do". An unhappy guest is your responsibility, whichever section they're in.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests want someone to own the problem.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, script: what to say

cards.prompt: "This was supposed to be hot, it's barely warm." What's the right first action?
options: Apologise, offer replacement dish, inform kitchen and manager.
answer: Apologise, offer replacement dish, inform kitchen and manager.
cards.explanation: For a cold or incorrect dish: apologise, replace it immediately and notify the kitchen. Taking it off the bill is a void, so a manager authorises it.
cards.why_it_matters: Acting fast shows the guest we care more about them than the bill.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, complaint scenario playbook; void and discount controls (David, 16 Oct 2026: voids need manager authorisation)
cards.review_note: Updated 16 Oct 2026: voids need manager authorisation (David).

cards.prompt: "We've waited 40 minutes and nothing's come out." What do you do?
options: Apologise and tell them it will be out in a few minutes
Acknowledge it, update them honestly and offer a complimentary item
Apologise and promise it's next out, whatever the kitchen says
Apologise and offer a complimentary item, without checking the kitchen
answer: Acknowledge it, update them honestly and offer a complimentary item
cards.explanation: For a long wait: acknowledge, update the guest, offer a complimentary item. Escalate if the wait is over twice the normal time.
cards.why_it_matters: Honest updates calm guests far more than vague promises.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, complaint scenario playbook
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Which of these can you resolve yourself, without a manager? Pick all that apply.
options: A guest asking for a refund
Removing a single item from the bill
A guest saying the food made them ill
cards.explanation: You can replace a dish or drink, apologise and follow up, and adjust seating, noise or pace. Removing an item from the bill is a void and needs a manager, as do refunds and illness or injury.
cards.why_it_matters: Fixing small things on the spot keeps the guest's visit on track.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, resolve it or escalate it?; void and discount controls (David, 16 Oct 2026: voids need manager authorisation)
cards.review_note: Updated 16 Oct 2026: voids need manager authorisation (David). "Removing a single item from the bill" is now a wrong option.

cards.prompt: When you bring in a manager for a complaint, how do you hand over?
options: Tell the guest a manager is coming, then carry on
Bring the manager over and let the guest explain again
Brief the manager at the pass, then let them go over
Introduce the manager personally, with the full story
answer: Introduce the manager personally, with the full story
cards.explanation: Flag it early, hand over warmly by introducing the manager personally, and give them full context. Never disappear without a word.
cards.why_it_matters: The guest shouldn't have to repeat the problem.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, the escalation protocol
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest is getting louder. What helps calm things down?
options: Keep your voice firm so they know you're in charge
Stand close so you can talk more quietly
Lower your voice slightly and slow your pace
Explain the reason quickly before they get louder
answer: Lower your voice slightly and slow your pace
cards.explanation: Lower your voice and slow down: calm is contagious. Keep an open posture and give the guest space.
cards.why_it_matters: A calm voice is the quickest way to bring the temperature down.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, read the room
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: What are the four Maison Mathis brand pillars? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: Quality, Simplicity, Authenticity and Warmth.
cards.why_it_matters: The pillars explain why we do things the way we do.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, brand pillars; Service Training Program v2026/01, day 1
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: What does the "Swan Theory" ask of you during a busy service?
options: Keep moving so guests see you're busy
Stay graceful by slowing down when it's busy
Look calm and graceful while working fast
Work steadily, never faster than guests notice
answer: Look calm and graceful while working fast
cards.explanation: Appear calm and graceful always, working at full speed beneath the surface. Guests should never feel the pressure.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests relax when the team looks in control.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, our service philosophy
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: You pass an empty glass on a table in another waiter's section. What do you do?
options: Leave it; offering drinks belongs to their waiter
Clear it only if their waiter is busy
Let that waiter know so they can offer a refill
Offer a refill or clear it yourself
answer: Offer a refill or clear it yourself
cards.explanation: The Gentleman's Agreement: an empty glass, an uncleared table or a guest needing help is your responsibility, whatever your section.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests see one team, not sections.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, our service philosophy
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest asks something you don't know. What do you say?
options: "I think so, but I'm not sure"
"I'll check if I get a minute"
cards.explanation: Never say "I don't know" without immediately offering to find out. Then always follow up.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests trust a team that finds the answer.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, guest service standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (sample of 10), drafted by Claude 16 Oct 2026. Same facts and right answer; the new wrong options come from our own menus and standards.

cards.prompt: When can you use your personal phone on the floor?
options: Only at the side station, when it's quiet
Only for work calls, out of guests' sight
Only to check bookings or the rota
cards.explanation: No personal phone use on the floor.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests should always see a team that's focused on them.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, guest service standards; Operations Manual v2026/01, guest service standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: What does the pre-shift briefing cover? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: Every shift starts with a 15-minute briefing: specials, reservations, 86'd items, known VIPs, and one team focus.
cards.why_it_matters: Knowing these before the doors open stops surprises at the table.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, shift management
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.explanation: Every shift begins with a 15-minute team briefing.
cards.why_it_matters: It's the team's one chance to plan the shift together.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, shift management; Service Training Program v2026/01, shift management
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

options: Chairs left stacked until the first booking
Music set lively to fill the room

cards.why_it_matters: The first guest of the day deserves the same house as the hundredth.

cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, opening procedures
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: How often is the bakery display refreshed through the day?

cards.why_it_matters: A fresh display sells; a tired one doesn't.

cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: It's near closing and one table is still chatting over coffee. What do you do?
options: Let them finish without rushing them
Start closing tasks around them, quietly
Ask if they'd like the bill, as you're closing soon
Bring the bill so it's ready when they are

cards.explanation: At wind-down, give final tables a genuine farewell; remaining guests are not rushed.
cards.why_it_matters: The last guest's memory of us matters as much as the first's.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, closing procedures
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: When is handwashing mandatory? Pick all that apply.

cards.why_it_matters: Clean hands are the simplest way to protect guests.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, personal hygiene; Service Training Program v2026/01, personal hygiene

cards.prompt: A drink spills on the floor. What comes first?
options: Put out a wet floor sign straight away
Stand by it and warn guests until it's dry
Tell a manager, then fetch a mop
Wipe it up first, then put out a sign
answer: Put out a wet floor sign straight away
cards.explanation: Deploy a wet floor sign immediately after any spill, then clean it up.
cards.why_it_matters: A slip can injure a guest or a teammate in seconds.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, slip and trip prevention
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A teammate trips but isn't hurt. Does it need logging?
options: No, near misses are only mentioned at the next briefing
Only if they need first aid
Yes, but by the end of the week is fine
Yes, every incident and near miss is logged that day
answer: Yes, every incident and near miss is logged that day
cards.explanation: Every incident, however minor, is logged on the day it happens, and near misses are reported and reviewed.
cards.why_it_matters: Near misses show where the next accident could happen.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, incident reporting; Service Training Program v2026/01, first aid and incident reporting
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: You feel unwell with a stomach bug before your shift. What's right?
options: Handle food but wash your hands more
Work, but stay away from the kitchen
cards.explanation: Team members with any illness affecting food safety must not handle food.
cards.why_it_matters: It protects guests and teammates from getting ill.
cards.source_ref: Operations Manual v2026/01, personal hygiene
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0008_harder_sop), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A couple tells you it's their anniversary. How do you adjust your suggestions?
options: Suggest value options and sharing items for the table
Suggest a bottle, and a dessert to share
answer: Suggest a bottle, and a dessert to share

cards.why_it_matters: The right suggestion makes their occasion feel special.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Two guests at a business lunch keep checking their watches. How do you adjust?
options: Suggest a sharing starter while they decide
Keep suggestions quick; offer coffee to go
Suggest a bottle and a dessert to share
Explain the signature dishes in detail
answer: Keep suggestions quick; offer coffee to go
cards.explanation: Guests checking their watches are short on time, so keep suggestions quick and practical, and offer coffee to go.
cards.why_it_matters: Respecting their time is the best service you can give.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A family is reading the prices very carefully. How do you adjust?
options: Suggest value options and sharing items
Suggest premium upgrades as a little treat for them
Suggest the specials of the day
answer: Suggest value options and sharing items
cards.explanation: Budget-conscious guests: recommend value options and sharing items, and avoid pushing premium upgrades.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests who feel their budget is respected relax and enjoy their visit.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Guests tell you it's their first time at Maison Mathis. What fits best?
options: Mention the new dishes and what's changed since last month
Explain our signature dishes and house specialities
Leave them to explore the menu alone
answer: Explain our signature dishes and house specialities
cards.explanation: First-time visitors are curious and want guidance, so explain the signature dishes and house specialities.
cards.why_it_matters: A great first visit is how a guest becomes a regular.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest isn't drinking alcohol. What do you do with drinks suggestions?
options: Suggest mocktails and fresh juices as warmly as cocktails
Ask them why they're not drinking tonight
Skip drinks suggestions altogether so they don't feel awkward
answer: Suggest mocktails and fresh juices as warmly as cocktails
cards.explanation: Guests not drinking alcohol still want something special. Recommend mocktails, fresh juices and premium waters with the same enthusiasm, and never make a guest explain.
cards.why_it_matters: Every guest deserves a great drink, with or without alcohol.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 5 and 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Regulars know the menu well. What should you suggest to them?
options: The signature dishes, explained in full detail again
The most expensive dish on the menu
Nothing; they already know what they want
New items and specials, and their favourites
answer: New items and specials, and their favourites
cards.explanation: Regulars know the menu, so mention new items and specials, and remember their favourites.
cards.why_it_matters: Remembering a regular's favourite makes them feel at home.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: What's the golden rule of selling?
options: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target
Focus on the items with the best margin
Suggest something on every visit to the table
Always offer the premium option first
answer: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target
cards.explanation: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target. A guest who feels looked after will return; a guest who feels pushed will not.
cards.why_it_matters: Long-term, loyal guests are worth far more than one bigger check.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest is showing signs of having had too much to drink. Their glass is empty. What do you do?
options: Suggest a lighter beer, like Hoegaarden
Offer a smaller measure or a lighter drink instead of a full one
Ask if they'd like the same again
Don't suggest another drink; follow responsible service rules
answer: Don't suggest another drink; follow responsible service rules
cards.explanation: Never suggest another round to a guest showing signs of intoxication. Follow responsible service rules and the venue's licensing conditions.
cards.why_it_matters: Guest safety and our licence come before any sale.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest with a nut allergy asks which dessert you'd recommend. What do you do?
options: Say you can't recommend any desserts
Recommend a dessert that has no nuts listed anywhere on the menu
Recommend the Dame Blanche straight away
Confirm with the kitchen first, then recommend a safe option
answer: Confirm with the kitchen first, then recommend a safe option
cards.explanation: Always check allergies before recommending and confirm with the kitchen if you're unsure. Never guess, then recommend a safe option with genuine enthusiasm.
cards.why_it_matters: An allergy can be life-threatening, and the menu doesn't show every ingredient.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 7 and 9.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality). Allergen card: needs the kitchen check.

cards.prompt: Which tables should you offer upgrades to?
options: Only the tables that look like they're big spenders
Only regulars who know the menu
cards.explanation: Never assume who can or can't afford an upgrade. Offer options respectfully to every table.
cards.why_it_matters: Judging a guest's budget is the quickest way to lose their trust.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Before service, what should you check with the kitchen so you don't sell the unavailable?
options: Tonight's table plan and the reservations list
cards.explanation: Check with the kitchen before service for 86'd (sold-out) items and preparation times.
cards.why_it_matters: Recommending a dish that's sold out disappoints the guest twice.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: What is suggestive selling?
options: Recommending a better version of what they've already ordered
Recommending the most expensive dish on the menu
Recommending today's special to every table
Recommending items the guest hadn't planned to order
answer: Recommending items the guest hadn't planned to order
cards.explanation: Suggestive selling recommends additional items the guest hadn't planned to order, to add to what they're already having. Upselling is upgrading what they've chosen.
cards.why_it_matters: Knowing the difference helps you pick the right technique at the right moment.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 2.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Suggestive selling mainly increases which part of the check?
cards.explanation: Suggestive selling adds more things; upselling makes each thing better.
cards.why_it_matters: A simple way to remember which technique you're using.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 2.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which of these are suggestive selling? Pick all that apply.
options: Suggesting Patatas Bravas to share while they decide
Offering the Black Angus Tenderloin instead of the Steak and Fries
Suggesting a large bottle of water for the table
Offering Hendrick's in the guest's gin and tonic
answer: Suggesting Patatas Bravas to share while they decide
Suggesting a large bottle of water for the table
cards.explanation: Starters, waters and coffee are new items on the check, so they're suggestive selling. A premium gin or a better steak upgrades something already ordered, so that's upselling.
cards.why_it_matters: Each technique has its own best moment in the meal.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 2.2 and 9.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Put these suggestions in the order they come during a meal.
options: A signature drink at the greeting
A sharing starter as you present the menu
A dessert as you clear the mains
A side dish with the main order
A second round at the mid-meal check-in
answer: A signature drink at the greeting
A sharing starter as you present the menu
A side dish with the main order
A second round at the mid-meal check-in
A dessert as you clear the mains
cards.explanation: Greeting: drinks. Menu: starters to share. Mains: sides. Mid-meal: another round. Clearing mains: dessert. After dessert: coffee or tea.
cards.why_it_matters: Suggesting an item just before the guest would think of it is what makes it welcome.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: You're clearing the mains. Which suggestion fits this moment best?
options: Another round of the same drinks
cards.explanation: Clearing the mains is the moment for dessert. Coffee, tea and digestifs come after dessert.
cards.why_it_matters: The right suggestion at the right moment feels like good service, not selling.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which is the strongest starter suggestion?
options: "Our starters are all really good, any you like the look of?"
"Have you tried our Van Tricht croquettes? Crispy, with an aged gouda inside."
"Would anyone like to have a look at our starters before you choose your mains tonight?"
"Would anyone like a starter tonight, or straight to mains?"
answer: "Have you tried our Van Tricht croquettes? Crispy, with an aged gouda inside."
cards.explanation: Name a specific item and describe one or two qualities. Vague questions get vague answers, usually "no".
cards.why_it_matters: A specific dish creates a picture in the guest's mind.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which dessert question works best?
options: "Will it be dessert, or just the bill for you?"
"Would you like the Dame Blanche or the Tarte Tatin to finish?"
"You really should have a dessert tonight, they're all really great."
answer: "Would you like the Dame Blanche or the Tarte Tatin to finish?"
cards.explanation: Offer a choice, not a yes/no question: it invites the guest to choose rather than refuse.
cards.why_it_matters: "Which would you prefer?" is easier to answer than "Do you want...?"
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Why suggest a starter for the table to share, rather than one each?
options: It's quicker to write on the pad
Sharing feels like less of a commitment
Guests always want to try each other's food
The kitchen prefers to cook sharing plates
answer: Sharing feels like less of a commitment
cards.explanation: Sharing items feel lower-commitment, so "Shall I bring one to share?" is easier to say yes to than asking each guest.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests say yes more easily when it doesn't feel like a big decision.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: What makes a personal recommendation work?
options: You've tasted it and genuinely like it
It's the dish the team needs to sell most
It's the most expensive dish on the menu
answer: You've tasted it and genuinely like it
cards.explanation: Only recommend things you've tasted and genuinely like. Guests can tell when enthusiasm isn't genuine.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests trust honest, personal opinions.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 3.2 and 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which words help a guest imagine how a dish tastes?
cards.explanation: Sensory words like crispy, slow-cooked, chargrilled and house-made help guests imagine the taste. Describe one or two qualities, not the full recipe.
cards.why_it_matters: A dish the guest can picture is a dish they want.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 3.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which phrase should you avoid when taking an order?
cards.explanation: Avoid closed phrases like "Is that all?" or "Do you want anything else?". Use specific, inviting ones like "Have you tried our...?"
cards.why_it_matters: A closed question invites a "yes, that's all".
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 6
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest politely declines dessert. What do you do?
options: Ask "Are you sure?" in case they change their mind
Accept it, and offer coffee or mint tea just once
Leave the dessert menu on the table, just in case
Describe the desserts again in more detail
answer: Accept it, and offer coffee or mint tea just once
cards.explanation: Accept a no graciously and offer a lighter alternative only once. Repeating a suggestion after a no damages trust.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest who feels respected comes back.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 7 and 9.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: How many items should you recommend at once?
options: A whole section of the menu
cards.explanation: Too many options overwhelm guests. Recommend one or two items.
cards.why_it_matters: A clear recommendation is easier to say yes to.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: When is it too late to suggest a starter?
options: Once the mains have been ordered
While you take the table's drinks order
While the guests read the menu
answer: Once the mains have been ordered
cards.explanation: Timing matters: offering starters after the mains are ordered, or dessert while guests are still eating, comes too late or too early.
cards.why_it_matters: Suggestions only work when they fit the flow of the meal.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Of the five habits of a great seller, which means "suggest once, respect the answer"?
cards.explanation: The five habits are Taste, Read, Describe, Time and Respect. Respect means suggest once, respect the answer, and always put the guest first.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest who feels looked after will return; one who feels pushed won't.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 10
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Put the barista's steps in order.
options: Turn on equipment and set up
answer: Turn on equipment and set up
cards.explanation: Set up, check the coffee quality, check KOTs, prepare, serve, then restock.
cards.why_it_matters: A set routine keeps every cup to standard through the rush.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), steps 1 to 6

cards.prompt: Before extracting a coffee, how long do you purge water from the group head?
cards.explanation: Release or purge water for 2 seconds from the group head before extracting coffee.
cards.why_it_matters: A clean, stable group head gives a better-tasting shot.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), step 2 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: You have a cappuccino and a latte to make. Which first, where possible?
options: Both from one jug, then split it
The cappuccino, to use the foam
The latte, so the milk is fresher
The latte, to stretch the milk first
answer: The cappuccino, to use the foam
cards.explanation: Where possible, make cappuccinos before lattes so the foam gets used.
cards.why_it_matters: Less waste, and both drinks get the right milk texture.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), step 4 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Several KOTs print at once. In what order do you make them?
options: In the order received, one ticket at a time
Hot drinks first, then cold, across tickets
In the order received, reading ahead
answer: In the order received, reading ahead
cards.explanation: Prepare orders in the order received, and read ahead to make several checks at once.
cards.why_it_matters: First come, first served is fair, and reading ahead saves time.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), step 3
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Two lattes are ready and no waiter has come for them. What do you do?
options: Call out the table number, then start the next ticket
Remake them when the waiter arrives, so they're hot
Let the waiters know politely, or run them yourself
Keep them on the pass until their waiter returns
answer: Let the waiters know politely, or run them yourself
cards.explanation: Serve hot drinks immediately: let the waiters know politely, or run them yourself whenever possible.
cards.why_it_matters: Coffee that sits goes cold and comes back to be remade.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), step 5
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Setting up the coffee station: what do you do? Pick all that apply.
options: Switch the machine on at the first order
Make a test espresso and check the flow
Pre-pour milk into jugs for the day
answer: Make a test espresso and check the flow
cards.explanation: Turn on and check pressure and temperature, warm cups, calibrate with a test espresso, and keep spare printer rolls ready.
cards.why_it_matters: Getting set up right before the first order keeps the rush smooth.
cards.source_ref: SOS Barista (Sequence of Service, Barista), steps 1 to 3; Operations Manual v2026/01, espresso calibration
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Put the host's steps in order, from opening the desk to seating guests.
cards.explanation: Set up the desk, acknowledge the guest, welcome them, seat them, hand menus, then go straight back to the desk.
cards.why_it_matters: Every guest gets the same warm start, however busy the door is.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), steps 1 to 6

cards.prompt: You're helping a guest at the desk when a couple walks in. What do you do?
options: Smile and let them know you've seen them
Finish with your guest first, then greet them
Call a waiter over to greet them
Excuse yourself and seat them straight away
answer: Smile and let them know you've seen them
cards.explanation: Give every guest immediate acknowledgement with a warm smile, even while you're attending to someone else.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest who knows they've been seen will wait happily.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 2; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 1
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A regular, Mr Khan, arrives for breakfast. How do you welcome him?
options: "Good morning, how many are you today?"
"Good morning sir, lovely to see you again"
"Good morning, welcome back! Table for one?"
cards.explanation: If guests have been before, greet them by name: "welcome back Mr X".
cards.why_it_matters: Using a regular's name makes them feel at home, which is why they keep coming back.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 3; Service Training Program v2026/01, guest service standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Which table should you choose for arriving guests?
options: The best table for their group size and type
A table in the busiest section, so the room looks full
A table by the window, whatever the group
The table nearest the host desk
answer: The best table for their group size and type
cards.explanation: Take guests to the best table for their group size and type, for example families or business guests, and seat tables evenly through the restaurant.
cards.why_it_matters: Seating evenly stops one waiter being overloaded, so every table gets good service.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 4
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: One waiter's section is full and another is quiet. A family of four arrives. Where do you seat them?
options: The next table in the busy waiter's section
A suitable table in the quieter section
A table by the kitchen, away from other guests
Any free table, to seat them quickly
answer: A suitable table in the quieter section
cards.explanation: Seat tables evenly through the restaurant, choosing a table that suits a family of four.
cards.why_it_matters: An overloaded waiter means slower service for everyone in that section.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 4 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Guests are seated. What do you say as you hand over the menus?
options: "Enjoy, our specials are on the back"
"Let me know when you're ready to order"
cards.explanation: Hand open menus to the seated guests and tell them their waiter will be along shortly.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests relax when they know what happens next.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 5
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A family with a toddler sits down. What can you offer as you hand menus? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: Give any highchairs needed, plus a children's menu and a colouring sheet.
cards.why_it_matters: Settling the children first lets the whole family enjoy the visit.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 5

cards.prompt: The restaurant is full and guests are waiting. What should you do?
options: Give a realistic waiting time and use a waiting list
Seat them at a table as soon as it's cleared, before it's reset
Quote a short wait so they don't walk away
Suggest they come back in an hour
answer: Give a realistic waiting time and use a waiting list
cards.explanation: When it's busy, be realistic about waiting times and keep a waiting list.
cards.why_it_matters: An honest wait is easier for guests than a broken promise.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 6
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: How do you answer the restaurant phone?
options: "Hello, this is Sara from Maison Mathis, who's calling please?"
"Good afternoon, thank you for calling Maison Mathis, how can I help?"
"Good afternoon, Maison Mathis Arabian Ranches, this is Sara speaking"
"Maison Mathis Arabian Ranches, Sara speaking, please hold"
answer: "Good afternoon, Maison Mathis Arabian Ranches, this is Sara speaking"
cards.explanation: Greet with the time of day, Maison Mathis and the location name, then your own name, and ask "How can I help you?"
cards.why_it_matters: The phone is often a guest's first contact with the house.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 7
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest calls to book a table. What do you do with their details?
options: Take their name and time, and remember the rest
Enter the booking straight into the system without repeating it back
Ask their name, write the details down and repeat them back
Write down the time and party size, then thank them
answer: Ask their name, write the details down and repeat them back
cards.explanation: Ask the guest's name, take the details, write them down and repeat them back, then thank them for calling.
cards.why_it_matters: Repeating details back catches mistakes before the guest arrives.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 7
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: The phone rings while you're with a guest at the desk. What's right?
options: Let it ring; the guest in front of you comes first
Excuse yourself politely and answer it
Answer it without stopping your conversation
Finish with your guest, then call the number back
answer: Excuse yourself politely and answer it
cards.explanation: If you're attending a guest when the phone rings, excuse yourself to answer it.
cards.why_it_matters: Both guests feel looked after: the one in front of you and the one calling.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 7 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Setting up the host desk: what do you check? Pick all that apply.
options: Today's reservations, with booked tables assigned
Menus stocked, with specials and promo menus
The waiting area and front entrance are clean
answer: Today's reservations, with booked tables assigned
Menus stocked, with specials and promo menus
The waiting area and front entrance are clean
cards.explanation: Check the reservations diary and assign booked tables, stock menus with specials and promo menus, and check the entrance and waiting area as a guest would see them.
cards.why_it_matters: The door is the guest's first impression of the house.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 1

cards.prompt: Why does the host check the toilets often?
options: Because the cleaners finish at noon
To count how many guests are inside
Guests link toilet cleanliness with our kitchens
answer: Guests link toilet cleanliness with our kitchens
cards.explanation: Check the toilets often: guests associate their cleanliness with the cleanliness of our kitchens.
cards.why_it_matters: A clean bathroom tells guests they can trust the food.
cards.source_ref: SOS Host (Sequence of Service, Host), step 6 tip

cards.prompt: Put the food runner's steps in order.
cards.explanation: Set up the pass, check the KOT and prepare the tray, run, serve, offer condiments, check the order is complete, then return to the pass.
cards.why_it_matters: The same routine every run means the right food reaches the right guest, hot.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), steps 1 to 7

cards.prompt: As you load a tray, what do you check against the KOT?
options: Each dish, plus the drinks ordered by the table at the same time
Each dish, plus the bill for the table
Each dish and the table number, nothing else
Each dish, table number plus any spoons or steak knives needed
answer: Each dish, table number plus any spoons or steak knives needed
cards.explanation: Check off each item on the KOT as it goes on the tray, including spoons or steak knives.
cards.why_it_matters: A missing knife or side means the guest waits while others eat.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 2
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A table of six is ready and you can't carry it all. What do you do?
options: Wait at the pass until a waiter is free
Take what you can now and come straight back
Get someone to help so it goes in one go
Ask the kitchen to hold half under the lights
answer: Get someone to help so it goes in one go
cards.explanation: Take the whole table's order in one go. If you can't, get someone else to help you.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests at one table should eat together.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 2
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Before a dish leaves the pass, what do you check?
options: The guest's name is on the KOT
It matches the photo on the menu
cards.explanation: Check every dish is garnished correctly before taking it from the pass.
cards.why_it_matters: The plate the guest sees should match the house standard every time.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 2 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Serving at the table: what's right? Pick all that apply.
options: Move around the table to each guest
Reach across guests to save time
Announce each dish as you serve it
Ask the table who ordered what
answer: Announce each dish as you serve it
Move around the table to each guest
cards.explanation: Announce each dish, move around the table rather than reaching over anyone, and warn about hot plates, keeping them away from children.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests feel looked after, and nobody gets burnt.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 4; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 5

cards.prompt: You drop a plate on the way to the table. What do you do?
options: Serve the rest, then tell the guest it's on its way
Get it replaced as a priority and tell your manager
Tell the guest, and let them choose something else
Get it replaced as a priority; no need to tell anyone
answer: Get it replaced as a priority and tell your manager
cards.explanation: If food is dropped or spilled, replace it as a priority and inform your manager.
cards.why_it_matters: The guest is already waiting; quick action keeps the delay short.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 6 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest asks you for another drink. What do you do?
options: Punch it in yourself at the nearest POS
Remember it and tell the waiter at the pass
Tell the bar, so it's made straight away
cards.explanation: If guests order more drinks, inform the relevant waiter immediately.
cards.why_it_matters: The guest asked once; they shouldn't need to ask again.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 7
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Walking back to the pass from a table, what should be in your hands?
options: Only your tray, to keep the pass moving
Any empty glasses, plates or cutlery
Empty glasses only; plates are for waiters
Nothing, so you're ready for the next run
answer: Any empty glasses, plates or cutlery
cards.explanation: Never leave a table empty-handed: remove any empty glasses, plates or cutlery.
cards.why_it_matters: Every trip keeps tables tidy without extra journeys.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 7 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest tells you their dish is too salty. Who do you tell?
options: The waiter only, so they can apologise
The chef in charge, and the waiter
The manager on duty, after the shift
No one unless the guest asks you to
answer: The chef in charge, and the waiter
cards.explanation: Liaise with the chef in charge and pass on any guest feedback about dishes.
cards.why_it_matters: The kitchen can only fix what it hears about.
cards.source_ref: SOS Food Runner (Sequence of Service, Food Runner), step 1 tip; Service Training Program v2026/01, guest recovery

cards.prompt: Put the first six steps of the sequence of service in order.
cards.explanation: Welcome, drink order, serve drinks, food order, serve food, then check the guests are enjoying their meal.
cards.why_it_matters: The same order every time means nothing is missed, however busy it gets.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), steps 1 to 6

cards.prompt: Put the last five steps of the sequence of service in order.
cards.explanation: Call the mains, clear, present the dessert menu, present the check, then see the guests off.
cards.why_it_matters: The end of the meal is what guests remember most, so it needs the same care as the start.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), steps 7 to 11
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: You reach a table and the guests are deep in conversation. What do you do?
options: Come back once they've stopped talking
Start your welcome so they know you're there
Wait for them to call you over
Wait a few seconds to catch their eye
answer: Wait a few seconds to catch their eye
cards.explanation: If the guests are talking, wait a few seconds to attract their attention. Never wait for a guest to approach you first.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests feel noticed without being interrupted.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: As you approach a table to introduce yourself, who do you make eye contact with?
options: The oldest guest at the table
cards.explanation: Make eye contact with the host as you approach the table, then introduce yourself as soon as possible.
cards.why_it_matters: The host is the person looking after the table's guests, so they should feel looked after first.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Entering a drinks order into Micros, what do you double-check? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: Double-check the table number, the number of guests, and that the order went in correctly with every special request.
cards.why_it_matters: A mistyped table number sends the drinks to another table.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: How do you pick up a glass to serve it?
options: By the base or the stem
With a napkin around the bowl
By the body, away from the rim
By the rim, so it stays steady
answer: By the base or the stem
cards.explanation: Pick up the glass by the base or stem, never the rim, with clean, dry hands and no fingerprints or lipstick marks on the glass.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests drink from the rim, so it must stay untouched.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 3
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: You arrive with a tray of drinks for a table. Who do you serve first?
cards.explanation: Serve ladies and older gentlemen first, announcing each drink as you serve it.
cards.why_it_matters: A consistent, courteous order is part of formal service.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 3
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: From which side of the guest do you serve drinks and food?
options: Drinks from the right, food from the left
Food from the right, drinks from the left
cards.explanation: Announce and serve drinks from the right, and approach the guest from the right to serve food.
cards.why_it_matters: Serving from one side every time means you never reach across a guest.

options: Ask "Is everything OK with your drinks?"
Ask if they're ready to order food
Step back and say "Enjoy your drinks!"
Leave quietly so you don't interrupt
answer: Step back and say "Enjoy your drinks!"
cards.explanation: When everyone has been served, take a step back and say "Enjoy your drinks!"
cards.why_it_matters: A small, warm close makes the moment feel finished.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 3
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: What must you do before leaving the table with a food order?
options: Repeat the order back to each guest
Check it on the POS while at the table
Read the whole order back to the host
Confirm the total with the host
answer: Repeat the order back to each guest
cards.explanation: Repeat the order back to each guest with eye contact. You must be 100% sure the order is understood and recorded correctly before you leave.
cards.why_it_matters: Repeating it back catches mistakes before the kitchen starts cooking.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 4
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Taking the food order, what must you find out from your guests? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: Collect all the information you need, such as allergies and dietary requirements, and explain dishes so guests know what they're ordering.
cards.why_it_matters: An allergy missed at the order can't be fixed once the dish is cooked.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 4

cards.prompt: What's the most plates you should carry at one time?
