cards.explanation: Never carry more than 3 plates at a time, and hold them straight so no sauce spills.
cards.why_it_matters: Fewer plates means no spills and no dropped food at the table.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: You're about to serve a plate but the guest hasn't seen you. What do you say?
options: Nothing; wait until they notice you
cards.explanation: Approach from the right, and if the guest doesn't see you, say "May I?"
cards.why_it_matters: It avoids startling the guest or knocking into them.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Serving sauces or condiments, what do you tell the guest?
options: Name, price and whether it's spicy
cards.explanation: Serve the sauces or condiments and explain what they are: name, ingredients and spiciness.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests can't enjoy a sauce they're unsure about, especially if it's hot.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Before taking plates to a table, what do you check them against?
cards.explanation: Double-check the food against the captain order, make sure plates are clean of drips and fingerprints, and that you have the right condiments.
cards.why_it_matters: Catching a missing or mixed-up dish at the pass saves the guest a wait.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 5
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: How often must you check on each table's satisfaction during a meal?
options: Only if they call you over
cards.explanation: Visit each table at least once during the meal to check the guests are enjoying their food and drinks.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests who aren't happy often won't say so unless you ask.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 6
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: A guest complains about a dish. How should you see it?
options: As something for the manager to handle
As a one-off to apologise for and move on
As feedback to pass to the kitchen later
As a second chance to win them back
answer: As a second chance to win them back
cards.explanation: A guest who complains gives you a second chance, unlike guests who say nothing and never return, so do whatever it takes to recover them.
cards.why_it_matters: A complaint handled well can win a guest for life.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 6
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: How do you know when to call the main course?
options: Watch how fast the table is eating
Once all the starter plates are cleared
As soon as the starters are served
When the guests ask for their mains
answer: Watch how fast the table is eating
cards.explanation: Monitor the meal, estimate how fast the guests are eating, then go to the service station and send the mains away.
cards.why_it_matters: Good timing means mains arrive just as guests are ready, not too soon or too late.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Clearing a plate, how do you hold the cutlery?
options: Knife handle to your thumb, thumb on it, fork slid under the knife
Fork handle to your thumb, thumb on it, knife slid under the fork
Fork handle to your thumb, knife laid on top of the fork
Fork and knife side by side, held under your fingers
answer: Fork handle to your thumb, thumb on it, knife slid under the fork
cards.explanation: Turn the fork handle towards your thumb and hold it down with your thumb, then slide the knife underneath the fork so nothing slides around.
cards.why_it_matters: Cutlery that can't move won't fall on a guest or the floor.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 8
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Guests stand up to leave while you're in the middle of a task. What do you do?
options: Nod and smile, then carry on
Pause to thank them and say goodbye
Finish your task, then wave as they go
Leave the farewell to the host at the door
answer: Pause to thank them and say goodbye
cards.explanation: Even mid-task, pause briefly to thank the guests, get their feedback and say goodbye.
cards.why_it_matters: The last moment is often the one guests remember.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 11
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: Guests have just left. Where do you check for anything they've forgotten?
options: On the table and the chairs, and by the entrance
On the table, on the chairs and under the table
answer: On the table, on the chairs and under the table
cards.explanation: Check on top of the table, on the chairs and below the table so guests don't forget anything.
cards.why_it_matters: Catching a phone or bag before the guest reaches their car saves a stressful trip back.
cards.source_ref: Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026), step 11
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Sequence of service steps, 11-step document (from David, 20 Oct 2026).

cards.prompt: How quickly must every guest be acknowledged on arrival?
cards.explanation: Every guest is acknowledged within 30 seconds of arrival, with eye contact and a smile.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest who knows they've been seen will wait happily.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: How soon after seating should water be served?
cards.explanation: Offer still or sparkling water on seating; water is served within 3 minutes.
cards.why_it_matters: Water first makes guests comfortable straight away.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: What's the standard for serving a cocktail after it's ordered?
cards.explanation: Other drinks are served within 5 minutes; cocktails take up to 8 minutes.
cards.why_it_matters: Drinks set the pace for the whole meal.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (sample of 10), drafted by Claude 16 Oct 2026. Same facts and right answer; the new wrong options come from our own menus and standards.

cards.prompt: How soon after arrival should the food order be taken?
cards.explanation: Take the food order within 10 minutes of arrival.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests notice a slow start more than almost anything else.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Starters are ordered. How long until they should be served?
cards.explanation: Starters are served within 15 minutes.
cards.why_it_matters: Knowing the standard helps you spot a delay early.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (sample of 10), drafted by Claude 16 Oct 2026. Same facts and right answer; the new wrong options come from our own menus and standards.

cards.prompt: A table ordered mains only, no starters. When should the mains arrive?
cards.explanation: Mains come 10 minutes after starters are cleared, or within 20 minutes when there are no starters.
cards.why_it_matters: You can update the guest honestly if the kitchen is running late.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards

cards.prompt: Food has just been served. When do you check back?
cards.explanation: Check back within 2 minutes of the food being served.
cards.why_it_matters: If there's a problem, two minutes in is early enough to fix it.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards; Operations Manual v2026/01, check-backs
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (sample of 10), drafted by Claude 16 Oct 2026. Same facts and right answer; the new wrong options come from our own menus and standards.

cards.prompt: A guest asks for the bill. What are the standards?
options: Present it within 5 minutes, payment done within 3
Present it within 2 to 3 minutes, payment done within 5
Present it within 3 minutes, payment done within 10
Present it within 5 minutes, payment done within 10
answer: Present it within 2 to 3 minutes, payment done within 5
cards.explanation: Present the bill within 2 to 3 minutes of the request and finalise payment within 5.
cards.why_it_matters: The last minutes of a visit shape how guests remember it.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 6; Sequence of service steps, 11-step document, step 10; David, 20 Oct 2026 (bill within 2 to 3 minutes)
cards.review_note: Updated 20 Oct 2026: bill within 2 to 3 minutes of the request (David).

cards.prompt: Put these in the order they should happen for a table.
cards.explanation: Water within 3 minutes, food order within 10, bread within 5 minutes of the order, then check back 2 minutes after food is served.
cards.why_it_matters: Each step sets up the next one, so the meal flows.
cards.source_ref: Service Training Program v2026/01, key timing standards

cards.prompt: Put the waiter's steps in order.
cards.explanation: Welcome, drinks, food order, food delivery and check back, clearing, desserts and coffees, then bill and goodbye.
cards.why_it_matters: Following the same order every time means nothing is forgotten when it's busy.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), steps 1 to 7

cards.prompt: Guests walk in and the host is busy. Who welcomes them?
options: The host, once free; others carry on serving
The manager on duty, if the host is busy
The waiter whose section they'll sit in
cards.explanation: Don't rely on the host to welcome guests: it is everyone's responsibility.
cards.why_it_matters: Every guest should be acknowledged within 30 seconds, whoever is nearest.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 1 tip; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 1
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Taking the drinks order, what else do you tell guests?
options: How long the kitchen is taking today
Today's specials and anything out of stock
The prices of the premium drinks
That food orders are taken within 10 minutes
answer: Today's specials and anything out of stock
cards.explanation: Ask "can I get you something to drink?" and tell guests about daily specials and any out-of-stock items.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests shouldn't fall for a dish, then hear it's not available.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 2; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 2
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A table orders soft drinks. What do you also suggest?
cards.explanation: Suggest bottled water to every table, whatever else they order, offering still or sparkling.
cards.why_it_matters: Water arrives first and keeps guests comfortable while they wait for food.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 2 tip; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 2

cards.prompt: You've punched a food order. What do you take to the table straight away?
cards.explanation: Repeat the order back, punch it straight away and take the bread tin to the table. Bread is served within 5 minutes of the order.
cards.why_it_matters: Fresh bread is part of the house welcome and fills the wait for starters.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 3; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 4
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: When you take the food order, what must you ask every table?
cards.explanation: At the food order, ask "does anyone have any allergies?" If they do, tell the head chef straightaway. Never guess.
cards.why_it_matters: Asking every time is how we catch an allergy before the food is cooked.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 3 (allergen line added 16 Oct 2026); Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 4

cards.prompt: A guest orders the Steak and Fries 200 gr. How do you suggest a side?
options: "Would you like a sauce with it, like béarnaise or peppercorn?"
"Would you like Crispy Truffle Fries or a Garden Salad with that?"
"Would you like any sides with that?"
"Can I get you something on the side, maybe some vegetables or salad?"
answer: "Would you like Crispy Truffle Fries or a Garden Salad with that?"
cards.explanation: Suggest side dishes by name to complement the main. Knowing the sides list makes this easy.
cards.why_it_matters: A named suggestion helps the guest picture it, so it's easier to say yes.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 3 tip; AR lunch and dinner menu, Sides
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A guest is eating the Steak and Fries. What's the best check-back question?
options: "Is everything OK?" as you walk past
cards.explanation: Ask about the dish by name, such as "How is your steak?" "How are you enjoying your meal?" is fine too, but naming the dish shows real interest.
cards.why_it_matters: Catching a problem early prevents a complaint and protects our reviews.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 4; Sequence of service steps, 11-step document, step 6; David, 20 Oct 2026 (naming the dish preferred, both accepted)
cards.review_note: Updated 20 Oct 2026: naming the dish is preferred; "How are you enjoying your meal?" is also accepted (David).

cards.prompt: When you check back on a table, what else do you do? Pick all that apply.
cards.explanation: At the check back, offer more drinks and remove any empty glasses.
cards.why_it_matters: An empty glass is a missed chance to look after the guest.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 4 tip
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: One guest has pushed their plate aside; the others are still eating. What do you do?
options: Ask the table if they're done
cards.explanation: Clear when everyone has finished, but if someone pushes their plate to the side first, you can remove it.
cards.why_it_matters: The guest has signalled they're done, and the table stays tidy.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 5 tip

cards.prompt: A guest has food left and says it was lovely. What do you offer?
options: To take it back to the kitchen to warm up
To pack the leftovers for them
answer: To pack the leftovers for them
cards.explanation: After asking "how was everything?", clear the plates and pack any leftovers for the guest.
cards.why_it_matters: They take the meal home and remember us later.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 5
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: Mains are cleared. How do you start desserts?
options: A dessert menu each, your favourite, and offer coffees
A dessert menu each, then come back for the order in 5 minutes
A dessert menu each, and ask if they'd like the bill
One dessert menu for the table, and offer coffees
answer: A dessert menu each, your favourite, and offer coffees
cards.explanation: Hand a dessert menu to each guest, say "my favourite dessert is the..." and offer coffees.
cards.why_it_matters: A personal recommendation is the friendliest way to suggest dessert.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 6
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: A table says they're too full for dessert. What could you suggest?
cards.explanation: Invite guests to visit the bakery counter for more cakes and desserts.
cards.why_it_matters: Takeaway from the bakery lets them enjoy it later.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 6 tip; Operations Manual v2026/01, bakery takeaway

cards.prompt: When should the bill be ready?
options: Printed when the table orders dessert
Checked and ready as soon as the table asks
Printed after they ask, then checked at the till
Brought with the last course, to save time
answer: Checked and ready as soon as the table asks
cards.explanation: Watch tables close to finishing, check their bill details and present it in a bill wallet as soon as they ask.
cards.why_it_matters: Waiting for the bill is one of the commonest reasons for a slow-service complaint.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 7; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 6
cards.review_note: Harder wrong options (0007_harder_service), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.

cards.prompt: When does a guest stop being our guest?
cards.explanation: Guests are our guests until they leave, not only until they pay. Thank them and say "see you again soon".
cards.why_it_matters: A warm goodbye is as important as a warm welcome.
cards.source_ref: SOS Waiter (Sequence of Service, Waiter), step 7 tip; Service Training Program v2026/01, sequence step 6

cards.prompt: What is upselling?
options: Suggesting a higher-value version of what the guest is ordering
Adding a service charge for premium items
Suggesting the most expensive item to every guest
Suggesting an extra item that the guest hadn't planned to order
answer: Suggesting a higher-value version of what the guest is ordering
cards.explanation: Upselling encourages a higher-value version of something already being ordered: a premium brand, larger size, better cut or an add-on.
cards.why_it_matters: Upselling raises the value of each item, not the number of items.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 2.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which question is typical of upselling?
options: "Can I get you anything else with that?"
cards.explanation: Upselling asks "Would you prefer the... instead?"; suggestive selling asks "Would you like to add...?"
cards.why_it_matters: The question shows which technique you're using.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 2.2 and 10
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which of these are upselling? Pick all that apply.
options: Guest orders a gin and tonic; you offer it with Hendrick's
Guest orders mains only; you suggest Patatas Bravas to share
Guest orders the Steak and Fries; you offer the Black Angus Tenderloin instead
Mains are cleared; you suggest the Dame Blanche
Guest orders the Signature Burger; you suggest adding pork bacon
answer: Guest orders the Steak and Fries; you offer the Black Angus Tenderloin instead
Guest orders a gin and tonic; you offer it with Hendrick's
Guest orders the Signature Burger; you suggest adding pork bacon
cards.explanation: A better cut, a premium gin and an add-on all raise the value of something the guest already chose. A new starter or dessert is suggestive selling.
cards.why_it_matters: Knowing which is which helps you choose the right moment for each.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 2.3, 4.1 and 9.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: You suggest adding cheddar (AED 5) to a guest's Veggie Burger. Which technique is that?
cards.explanation: Add-ons to an item the guest already chose, like extra cheese on a burger, count as upselling because they raise that item's value.
cards.why_it_matters: Add-ons are the easiest upsell: the guest has already said yes to the dish.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 2.3 note and 9.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: When is the best moment to upsell?
options: After the order is in the POS
The moment the guest names the item
When you bring the food to the table
answer: The moment the guest names the item
cards.explanation: Upsell right when the guest names the item. Once the order is placed and you've walked away, the moment has gone.
cards.why_it_matters: An upgrade offered later means changing an order, which guests rarely do.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest orders a glass of wine at AED 45. Which upgrade are they most likely to accept?
cards.explanation: Offer one step up, not three. A guest ordering a AED 45 glass is more likely to accept a AED 60 option than a AED 150 one.
cards.why_it_matters: A small step feels like a treat; a big jump feels like pressure.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: An upgrade carries a supplement. When do you mention the price?
options: Not at all; it shows on the bill
cards.explanation: Be transparent: mention a supplement naturally when you suggest the upgrade, so the guest is never surprised by the bill.
cards.why_it_matters: A surprise on the bill turns a good meal into a complaint.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 4.2 and 7
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Which steak upsell is strongest?
options: "The Wagyu is our most expensive steak, if you like."
"Would you like the more expensive steak instead?"
"For something special, the Westholme Wagyu is beautifully marbled; it's AED 130 more."
"Most of our guests go for the Wagyu striploin these days; it's a very popular choice."
answer: "For something special, the Westholme Wagyu is beautifully marbled; it's AED 130 more."
cards.explanation: Explain the benefit to the guest, not just the price, and be clear about the supplement. The Wagyu striploin is AED 265; the Steak and Fries is AED 135.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests upgrade when they understand what they'll get.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest orders the Steak and Fries 200 gr (AED 135). What's the natural one-step upsell?
options: A second Steak and Fries to share
cards.explanation: Offer the next level up, not the most expensive: from the Steak and Fries, that's the Black Angus Tenderloin.
cards.why_it_matters: One step up feels like a natural treat, not a hard sell.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Two guests each order a glass of the same white wine and mention a second round. What do you suggest?
options: A cocktail for the second round
Two glasses now, and you'll check back later for the next
A glass of Champagne each instead
A bottle: better value, kept chilled at the table
answer: A bottle: better value, kept chilled at the table
cards.explanation: If guests plan a second glass each, a bottle works out better value and stays chilled at the table.
cards.why_it_matters: The guest gets better value and you save a trip to the bar.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), sections 2.3 and 4.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: Why does a pairing make an upsell easier?
options: It feels like expert advice, not a sales pitch
The kitchen prefers dishes in pairs
It always works out cheaper for the guest in the end
answer: It feels like expert advice, not a sales pitch
cards.explanation: Pairing an upgrade with something the guest already ordered makes it feel like expert advice rather than a sales pitch.
cards.why_it_matters: Guests welcome advice; they resist being sold to.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: A guest orders a latte. Which suggestion is an upsell?
options: A croissant to go with it
cards.explanation: An extra shot upgrades the latte the guest already chose, so it's upselling. A croissant is a new item, so it's suggestive selling.
cards.why_it_matters: Small coffee upgrades add up over a busy morning.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 4.1
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: What's the main risk of overdoing upselling?
options: The guest feels judged on budget or misled on price
The kitchen runs out of premium items
The bill takes longer to print
The guest feels pushed into ordering far too much food
answer: The guest feels judged on budget or misled on price
cards.explanation: Overdone upselling leaves guests feeling judged on budget or misled on price. Overdone suggestive selling makes them feel pushed into ordering too much.
cards.why_it_matters: Trust is harder to win back than a sale.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 2.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

cards.prompt: An anniversary couple orders two glasses of house wine. What's the best approach?
options: Suggest a bottle now, and a dessert to share later
Suggest a bottle, a starter and the Wagyu at once
Suggest the most expensive Champagne straight away
Serve the glasses and leave them to it
answer: Suggest a bottle now, and a dessert to share later
cards.explanation: Upsell the wine to a bottle at the moment they order, and suggest a shared dessert when the mains are cleared.
cards.why_it_matters: Well-timed suggestions make the occasion feel special without pressure.
cards.source_ref: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality), section 9.2
cards.review_note: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-20 from Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality).

snapshot.prompt: What is our standard spirit measure?
snapshot.source_ref: Cocktails and Mocktails Manual v2026/01, drink presentation standards; AR lunch and dinner menu, 20260922_MM-AR-LUNCHDINNER39, spirits (30 ML)
snapshot.explanation: Every bartender uses a jigger for exact measurements; the standard measure is 30 ml.
snapshot.why_it_matters: Every guest gets the same drink, and over-pouring costs the house money.

snapshot.prompt: What is our standard spirit measure?
snapshot.source_ref: Cocktails and Mocktails Manual v2026/01, drink presentation standards; AR lunch and dinner menu, 20260922_MM-AR-LUNCHDINNER39, spirits (30 ML)
snapshot.explanation: Every bartender uses a jigger for exact measurements; the standard measure is 30 ml.
snapshot.review_note: Harder wrong options (0010_harder_drinks), drafted by Claude 2026-10-17. Same facts and right answer.
snapshot.why_it_matters: Every guest gets the same drink, and over-pouring costs the house money.

snapshot.prompt: How much is a glass of wine?
snapshot.source_ref: Cocktails and Mocktails Manual v2026/01, drink presentation standards; AR lunch and dinner menu, 20260922_MM-AR-LUNCHDINNER39, wines (150 ML / 750 ML)
snapshot.explanation: Wine and sparkling wine by the glass is 150 ml.
snapshot.why_it_matters: Guests compare glass and bottle; know the measure.

snapshot.prompt: How much is a glass of wine?
snapshot.source_ref: Cocktails and Mocktails Manual v2026/01, drink presentation standards; AR lunch and dinner menu, 20260922_MM-AR-LUNCHDINNER39, wines (150 ML / 750 ML)
snapshot.explanation: Wine by the glass is 150 ml.
snapshot.why_it_matters: Guests compare glass and bottle; know the measure.

snapshot.prompt: What's the rule on pouring above the measure?
snapshot.source_ref: Cocktails and Mocktails Manual v2026/01, drink presentation standards
snapshot.explanation: Over-pouring is not accepted: every recipe is tested, and a drink made by one bartender must be made exactly the same by all others.
snapshot.why_it_matters: Consistency is what guests expect every time.

snapshot.prompt: What's the rule on pouring above the measure?
options: Up to 5 ml is fine when free-pouring
